<description>
In a JSON-RPC batch, an element that is not an object gets an error reply with the id and version of the element before it.

`ExecuteHTTPRPC` parses every element of a batch into the same request object, and `parse()` throws on a non-object before it sets `id` and `m_json_version`. For `[{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"getblockcount","id":"X"}, 2]` the reply has two objects with `"id":"X"`, one with a result and one with an error. If the first element is a notification, the error is dropped. I give each element its own copy of the request, which holds only the HTTP fields, so the error is the one the first element of a batch already gets. The new case in `interface_rpc.py` fails on master and passes with this change.
</description>
